full_judgment:
2. Short facts for disposal of the rule are  that the opposite party No. 2 as plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No.77 of 1979 in the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 5th Court Dhaka for partition and the suit was decreed in preliminary from 31-3-1981. After preliminary decree one Habibur Rahman was appointed as Advocate Commissioner for ascertaining in the share of each party and their possession. The Commissioner held a commission accordingly and submitted his report, wherein some irregularities were detected for which the report of the commissioner was rejected on 4-6-2000 in presence of all the party. Thereafter one Abdus Satter Howleder was appointed as Advocate Commissioner who submitted his report before the court, against which the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant No. 19(a)-19(c) filed written objection which was heard by the trial court and it was rejected. Then Mr Shah Alam was appointed as Advocate Commissioner and his report was accepted. At the time of hearing, the defendant No. 35 filed an application for a compact saham as the Advocate Commissioner allotted him 0.845 aujutangsha from separate plot being plot Nos. 651,652,667 (chita map No. 9,19,36). The defendant No. 35 wanted to get the said saham from chita plot No. 10 as compact Saham. The trial court rejected the petition on 30-11-2004. The defendant No.19(Icha) was allotted 5.06 decimals in chits plot No. 10 (plot No. 651). The said defendant has been residing therein for about 50 years constructing sami pucca structure connecting electricity, gas, water line connection. The defendant No. 19(Ka) was allotted 6.17 decimal from plot No. 652 (chita Plot No. 11,12,13,16) who has been residing therein by constructing a 2 storied building. Both the defendant No. 19(Ka) and (Kha) were allotted 10 decimals from the plot No. 666 (chita plot No. 31). Thus the defendant No. 19(Ka) and 19(Kha) has been allotted 21.48 decimals of land which is accepted by the court on 30-11-2004. The defendant Nos.19(ka)-19(ga) got a saham of 24 decimals of land in preliminary decree dated 31-3-1981. Thereafter the defendant No.35 again filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial court on 10-2-2005 praying for getting compact saham. After hearing, trial Court allowed the application filed by the defendant No. 35, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order petitioner preferred the Civil Revision before the District Judge under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure which was heard by the Additional District Judge 2nd Court Dhaka who affirmed the order passed by the trial Court. 

 11. It appears from the record that both the defendant No. 35 and defendant Nos. 19(Ka)- 19(ga) got a saham in preliminary decree dated 31-3-1981, at the time of hearing of the commission report the defendant No.35 prayed for a compact saham under the plot No.651, 652 contending that the commissioner allotted him a Saham under plot No. 667 which is not his purchased plot, the Joint District judge rejected the application filed by the defendant No. 35 on 31/11/2004. Thereafter another application was filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it was allowed. 

 12. The learned Joint District Judge while allowing the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure considered that the defendant No.35 was not a purchaser under the plot No. 677 and the commissioner violated the preliminary decree passed by the court for the reason the Joint District Judge reviewed his own order dated 31-11-2004 and allowed a compact saham in favour of defendant No. 35 by allotting the chita plot Nos. 9 and 10 and by allotting chita plot No.19/36 instead of chita plot No.10 in favour of the defendant No. 10(a), 19(ga). Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order passed by the trial court petitioner preferred revisional application under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected by the Additional District Judge. On the ground that the Joint District Judge found that the commissioner did not act in accordance with the preliminary decree and by virtue of his inherent power the trial court reviewed its own order dated 30-11-2004 to bring the preliminary decree in conformity with the judgment. 

 14. It appears that the defendant No. 35 prayed for a compact saham under the plot No. 651, 652 contending that commissioner allotted him a saham of 364 under plot No. 667 is not his purchased land. This matter is absolutely a matter of fact which was decided by the trial court to bring the preliminary decree in conformity with the judgment. 

 "Amendment of decree-When it can done-The Court can always amend the decree if there is a mistake that had crept in for bringing the decree in conformity with the judgment-Code of Civil Procedure".
